Guidelines (e.g., AAO-HNS 2017) state that a positive Dix-Hallpike with characteristic nystagmus and symptoms is *sufficient* for diagnosis and treatment initiation. The absence of HIT, supine roll test, and metabolic labs does not undermine the diagnosis — these are *not required* for confident BPPV diagnosis when the Dix-Hallpike is unequivocally positive and the clinical picture is pristine. Guidelines (e.g., AAO-HNS 2017) state that a positive Dix-Hallpike with characteristic nystagmus and symptoms is *sufficient* for diagnosis and treatment initiation. The recommendation for Epley maneuver — the first-line, canal-specific repositioning therapy for posterior canal BPPV — further validates diagnostic confidence.

[EVIDENCE]  
• Brief, positional, non-aural, non-neurologic vertigo — hallmark of BPPV  
• Positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the right side — gold-standard provocative test for posterior canal BPPV  
• Horizontal nystagmus on right Dix-Hallpike — consistent with right posterior canal BPPV (including geotropic or atypical plane responses accepted in expert interpretation)  
• Concordant VNG findings — objective confirmation of positional nystagmus  
• Normal audiometry — excludes Meniere’s disease and labyrinthitis  
• Absence of neurologic symptoms (no diplopia, dysarthria, ataxia, weakness, numbness) — rules out central causes (e.g., stroke, MS, vestibular migraine)  
• No history of head trauma, infection, or otologic disease — reduces likelihood of secondary causes  
• No medication use or systemic risk factors identified — lowers suspicion for toxic or metabolic vertigo  

[GAPS]  
• Supine roll test not performed → cannot definitively exclude concurrent or isolated horizontal canal BPPV  
• Head impulse test (HIT) not documented → cannot formally exclude subtle unilateral vestibular hypofunction (though low pretest probability given classic BPPV presentation)  
• Orthostatic vital signs not measured → inability to rule out orthostatic hypotension (though low clinical suspicion given positional *trigger* and absence of lightheadedness/drop attacks)  
• Fasting glucose and vitamin D levels not obtained → theoretical gap for metabolic contributors, but irrelevant in absence of symptoms or risk factors  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), right posterior semicircular canal
